title: The frame at the owner's width, priced: the bloom chain's second scene pass halves the fps at 3440 wide, the static base is drawn as hundreds of calls a pass, and the chain's tail now sums and converts in one full-screen pass
context: An extra-high-effort pass with a 90-minute budget (owner, 2026-11-06), given a generic 3D optimisation checklist (profile first; cull and remove waste; cut draw calls; LOD and mipmaps; compress assets; a lean update loop; shader variants; the quality-preserving rule) to evaluate against the game. Branch perf-pass-2026-11-06 (worktree ~/Dev/stalheart-perf) off overnight-2026-10-23 e527eff4. Measured first, in a headed Chrome on the M4 (the attached display is 3440x1440 at 50 Hz, dpr 1), sector 2 on the default build (THE DOME CITY, the wireframe, the Pearl set), with a scratch CDP probe that hooks renderBufferDirect and renderer.render through Object3D.prototype.onBeforeRender (draw calls per pass and per top-level object, the scene census, renderer.info) and reads the frame readout (state().performance: fps, frame ms, the GPU timer, calls, triangles). The chain's probe tap (postfx.tap) gained split modes to price its parts: noPassA, noBloomPass, noMsaa/msaa, byteA/halfFloatA, separateAdd/onePass, halfA/fullA.
outcome: THE PICTURE. At 1440x900 the game holds the display's 50 Hz (20.0 ms a frame) with the GPU at 19.7 ms of it: 8.2 ms for the scene drawn once, 11.5 ms for the bloom chain (the weighted scene drawn again plus the mip chain, the 4x multisampled final buffer and the two full-screen tails). At 3440x1353, this display's own width, the same scene runs at 19-24 fps (41-52 ms a frame, GPU 49-74 ms) with the chain and 50 fps capped without it (GPU 14.6 ms). The split at 3440: skipping pass A (the weighted scene render and the mips together) gives 27.5 ms a frame (gpu 22.9); skipping only the mip chain changes nothing (41.5 ms); the final buffer's 4x MSAA costs about 6 ms of frame; pass A's half-float targets cost nothing against 8-bit ones (41.1 vs 40.4 ms). So pass A is a second full rasterisation of the scene, about 14 ms of frame at this width, and the frame there is GPU-bound in scene fill, drawn twice by the per-group bloom's design (output = scene + bloom(scene x weights)): not the enemies, not the draw calls, not textures (the 124 GLBs embed none; the only textures are the sinkhole's four jpgs), not geometry compression (the build already meshopt-packs every model), not LOD (the far tiers exist), not shader variants (140 programs). DRAW CALLS: the scene draws 1,060 calls a pass at 1440x900 and 1,900 at 3440 (the wider view takes in the far sites); the static base alone is 616 to 1,400 of them (308 to 778 meshes under 'Story base', one call each a pass): only 13 of the 34 base-layout structures and none of the dome city carry batch: true. Isao is 49 meshes, the cargo 48 + 8 skinned, the rover 59 wire meshes, the hull 50. Two hazards stand in the way of batching the rest, found and not fixed here: mergeByMaterial (src/glbmodels.js) keeps only position, normal and uv, so every batched model with COLOR_0 (the solar complex, the bio cassettes, the greenhouse, the chip writer, the ammo) renders today with vertexColors on and no colour attribute (18 such meshes live in the scene; what the GPU reads for the missing attribute is the API's default); and batchStaticAsset merges the CACHED gltf.scene in place, so two structures from one URL (bio-a/b/c today; the four rockets if batched) share one root. THE CHANGE: the chain's tail. The sum scene + bloom used to go to a full-resolution half-float buffer and the OutputPass read it back for the display transfer; AddOutputPass (src/postfx.js, built from the vendored OutputShader by string replacement, test/postfx.mjs guards the anchors) sums the two textures and applies the same tone-mapping switch and sRGB transfer in one fragment. The old two-pass tail is kept disabled for the probe's 'separateAdd' split. Measured at 3440x1353 on the same frozen scene, old tail against new on the same page: 40.3 ms a frame (24.8 fps, gpu 46.3) to 38.4 ms (26.1 fps, gpu 45.7), about 1.9 ms a frame back, the same at 1440x900 in proportion; pixel comparison of the two tails on a paused frame (gl.readPixels of the 3440x1353 drawing buffer, 13.96M colour channels): no channel differs by more than 1 of 255, 47,784 (0.34 %) differ by exactly 1, the half-float rounding the old intermediate added; the same tail grabbed twice differs in 0 channels. The chain-off floor is unchanged (50 fps capped, gpu 14.6 ms). NOT DONE, FOR THE OWNER: pass A at half the device resolution ('halfA', priced: 37.0 ms a frame, 27.1 fps, gpu 43.1: only 1.4 ms more than the one-pass tail at full size, which says pass A's 14 ms is geometry and draw work, not pixel fill) is not output-identical: a 1 px line rasterised at half size weighs about twice as much in the bloom, so the lattice and the wireframes would glow harder; a window-size tier (bloom off or halved past a width), dynamic resolution, or one scene pass writing both colour and weighted colour (multiple render targets, every material patched) are the real levers at this width and each changes the picture or is a project of its own. Batching the base (output-identical once COLOR_0 and the custom attributes are kept per batch, hide/dark nodes preserved as pivots, and the cached scene cloned first) is the next cut that costs nothing to look at: about 300 calls a pass, mostly CPU.
alternatives: Rendering pass A at half resolution for everyone: measured, rejected as a default; a 1 px line at half size is a 2 px line's weight in the bloom, which the owner would see on the lattice. Offered as a knob with its price.
Dropping the final buffer's 4x MSAA (about 6 ms at 3440): the wireframe's anti-aliasing is the look; not done.
Pass A in 8-bit targets: measured as no gain (the half-float traffic is not the cost), not done; it would also clip emissives over 1.0.
Hiding, in pass A, objects whose weighted colour cannot pass the threshold: not done; they occlude the glow behind them, so the picture changes where a dark body stands in front of a lit one.
Batching the dome city and the rest of the base in this window: not done; mergeByMaterial drops COLOR_0 and batchStaticAsset mutates the cached scene, both of which need their own measured fix first.
Texture compression (KTX2), mipmaps, Draco: not applicable; the models carry no textures and the build already meshopt-packs them.
evidence: A, 1440x900 dpr 1, headed, sector 2: chain on 50 fps 20.0 ms gpu 19.7 calls 2,024 tris 3.40M cpuFrame 10.6 (81-164 alive); chain off 50 fps gpu 8.22 calls 1,072 tris 1.70M cpuFrame 8.8. Passes a frame: scene x2 (2,127 calls), 14 full-screen quads to targets, 1 to the screen.
B, 3440x1353 dpr 1, main tree e527eff4: chain on 19.4 fps 51.9 ms gpu 74.2 calls 3,879 tris 5.01M cpuFrame 50.3; chain off 50 fps 20.0 ms gpu 14.3 calls 1,856 cpuFrame 10.8.

C, 3440x1353, the split: normal 24.2 fps 41.7 ms gpu 49.1; noPassA 36.7 fps 27.5 ms gpu 22.9 calls 1,856; noBloomPass 24.5 fps 41.5 ms gpu 45.7; noMsaa 28.3 fps 35.4 ms gpu 43.6; msaa 24.9 fps 40.3; byteA 24.5 fps 41.1 ms gpu 48.0; halfFloatA 24.8 fps 40.4 ms gpu 48.7; chain off 49.9 fps 20.1 ms gpu 14.6.

Draw sources at 1440x900 (calls a frame over both passes / objects): Story base meshes 1,232 / 308; ISAO_LOD1 196 / 49; Cargo 192 / 48 (+32 / 8 skinned); yushi rover wire 118 / 59; the hull wire 100 / 50; the sinkhole quake 64 / 16 instanced; the planet lattice 24 / 6 at 2.28M tris. At 3440: Story base 2,805 / 778.

Census: 1,947 meshes, 73 instanced, 31 skinned, 33 lines, 6 points; 1,129 visible; 244 never frustum-culled; 550 materials (299 transparent; 1,614 double-sided, 30 of them transparent, drawn back then front); 1,444 geometries; 140-145 programs; 35 textures.
vertexColors without a colour attribute, live in the scene: 18 meshes under solar (8), bio-c, greenhouse, chips, ammo-a/b/c and the rest.

D, 3440x1353, the worktree with the one-pass tail, modes 7 s each: onePass 26.1 fps 38.4 ms gpu 45.7; separateAdd (the old tail) 24.8 fps 40.3 ms gpu 46.3; onePass again 26.1 fps 38.3 ms gpu 45.6; halfA 27.1 fps 37.0 ms gpu 43.1; fullA 26.2 fps 38.1 ms gpu 45.0; chain off 50 fps 20.1 ms gpu 14.6. PIXDIFF on the paused frame: old vs new max 1, differing 47,784 of 13,962,960 channels, over 1: 0, mean 0.0034; old vs old again: max 0, differing 0. Logs and JSON in the session scratchpad (perf/A-1440-dpr1, B-3440-dpr1, C-3440-split, D-3440-after).

node test/postfx.mjs: the sizing invariants and the one-pass tail's four anchors hold. npm test: 333 test programs passed; npm run check: architecture, the line ceiling (td-tab 5,340 under 5,450), the long-line budget and top-level placement hold. The browser suites were not run in this window.
